target_question: Applicability of modularity lifting theorems (Kisin, Gee-Kisin, Thorne, Allen-Khare-Thorne) to signature (2, 3, p) for p in {11, 13, 17}, residual representations, ramification, Hodge-Tate weights, and exact technical obstacles to full resolution.

findings.modularity_lifting_applicability: Applies unconditionally. The Frey curves are elliptic curves over Q (or base-changed), hence their l-adic representations are already modular (BCDT 2001, Kisin 2009).
findings.residual_representations: rho_p: Gal(Q_bar/Q) -> GL_2(F_p), det = chi_p. Absolutely irreducible for all p >= 11 (FNS 2020 Prop 2.4).
findings.ramification: Unramified outside {2, 3, p}. Unramified at all primes l | c (l != p). Crystalline/ordinary at p.
findings.hodge_tate_weights: HT = {0, 1} at all places v | p.
findings.core_obstruction: Modularity lifting only confirms modularity, but does not provide non-existence. The candidate newform space is non-empty for every p due to the permanent Catalan solution (3, -2, 1) and CM trivial solutions. The problem reduces to rational points on twisted modular curves X_E(p), where Chabauty breaks down for p=13 (g(X_0(13))=0) and p=17 ([K_E:Q]=18, [L_E:Q]=54 exceeds class group capacity).
